acceptance_criteria: The full existing test suite passes unchanged with the feature off.
With the HTML5 parser enabled, HTML5 tree construction is observable: implied tbody, auto-closed p/li/td, and nested-table recovery match the browser/HTML5 result instead of the libxml result.
The default path costs at most one boolean check per document creation; measured against a benchmark that reports legacy vs html5 timings from real fixtures.
Unsupported runtime (PHP < 8.4 / missing Dom\HTMLDocument), keepBrokenHtml, and unparsable input fall back to the legacy path instead of throwing.
behavior_anchors: HtmlDomParser::loadHtml -> createDOMDocument -> Dom\HTMLDocument::createFromString -> XML bridge -> $this->document (\DOMDocument) -> find()/html()
goal: Add opt-in HTML5 parsing through the PHP >= 8.4 Dom\HTMLDocument parser to HtmlDomParser, bridged into the existing \DOMDocument pipeline, with the libxml path unchanged and still the default.
non_goals: Do not change the default parsing path or its output for any existing input.
Do not change the public return types (getDocument(): \DOMDocument, getNode(): \DOMNode) or add an interface method to DomParserInterface.
Do not enable the HTML5 parser automatically; PR #146 showed the bridge cost is real and must stay opt-in.
Do not port the PHP-side node-by-node projection bridge from PR #146.
